learning_outcomes.text: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
Capacity and skill to plan and carry out experimental research, interpret results and reach conclusions in their field of study.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project and research and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Ability to apply engineering practice standards of their specialty.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Applies methods, techniques, regulations, etc., specific to the engineering profession in known contexts.

syllabus_topics: Experimental analysis of a gasoline engine
Analysis of connections and parameters of a three-phase system
Direct start of a three-phase motor
Geometry of tools for chip removal processes
Production cycle time and takt time
teaching_methods: Workshop and/or laboratory practices (individual or team)
Development, writing, and presentation of reports, documentation, audiovisual material, etc., related to projects/POPBLs (individual or team)

assessment_methods.method: Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Technical ability, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, technical presentation and defense
Observation of student participation and attitude in the proposed training activities

assessment_rules: Assessment of this subject is continuous, and there will be no final recovery tests. At the end of each practice, an evaluation and feedback will be provided, and aspects for improvement must be applied in subsequent practices to improve grades. The final grade for the subject will be the average of the six practices. All practices are compulsory. If a student does not complete a practice due to a justified absence, the grade for that practice will not be considered for the average. A maximum of two practices may be left incomplete.
